correctness.rationale: Parity criterion matches published Aronhold definition. Integer enumeration yields exactly 288 heptads; a selected 28-column submatrix has exact Bareiss determinant of absolute value 7. All columns sum 7, hence the generated lattice sits in a subgroup of index 7, while the determinant bounds its index by 7. Equality, SNF and the reconstruction statement follow. Both proof and verifier stay finite for the certificate while the lattice conclusion applies to all integral vectors.

value.rationale: The Aronhold systems are the canonical seven-bitangent sets used for reconstructing genus-three plane quartics. The integer-span criterion is a complete natural invariant distinguishing rational span from integral representability. It shows every bitangent difference is generated integrally and that there is precisely one global mod-seven obstruction, information neither the 2-design replication numbers nor the classical 288-count alone supplies. The explicit determinant certificate enables reuse for integral theta-characteristic constructions.
